title: detection-capability.v1
comment: Per-DETECTOR Detection Capability Manifest (plan 021 U1). One manifest describes ONE detector: what it needs to run, what it claims to detect, and the tests that back those claims. This is DISTINCT from deploy/central/capability-manifest.json, which is the DEPLOYMENT (producer->topic->consumer) capability manifest; do not conflate the two. Two rules this contract enforces: (1) status=verified_e2e requires at least one backing_tests.golden_pcap (encoded below as an if/then); (2) KTD5 claim/limitation consistency is a cross-field semantic rule checked in contracts/test_detection_capability.py, not expressible here.

status.comment: Maturity ladder. verified_e2e is the only status that, per the if/then below, requires golden-pcap backing.

required_capabilities.comment: Observation capability tokens the detector needs present (e.g. tls-handshake, ja4, payload-visible).

attack_techniques.comment: ATT&CK technique/sub-technique ids this detector claims to detect.

input_records.comment: Input record/table names the detector consumes (e.g. ndr.dns, ndr.flow).

features_used.comment: Named features/signals the detector reads off each input record.

evidence_produced.comment: The evidence record the detector emits and the fields it populates as evidence.

known_limitations.comment: Honest caveats. A limitation may name a `claim` (a capability token or ATT&CK id) it qualifies and mark it `unverified`; KTD5 (checked in the test) forbids asserting that same claim in required_capabilities/attack_techniques.

allOf.comment: Rule 1: a verified_e2e detector MUST carry at least one golden-pcap backing test.
